unmapped_findings: For ANT850 (AN850) the theoretical superimposed yield strength is σy = 926 MPa versus a measured actual value of 964 MPa (difference of 38 MPa), based on σ0 = 220 MPa, σg = 292 MPa, σd = 414 MPa and σOrowan = 0 MPa (Table 3).

The Orowan strengthening contribution for this steel is 0 MPa because the Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitation strengthening occurs; retained austenite content is <5 % and its strengthening contribution is neglected.
GA optimisation of the Extra Trees model reduced the YS prediction difference at 850 °C by 17 MPa (from 36 MPa for plain Extra Trees to 19 MPa for GA-Extra Trees).
ANT850 GND density is 0.72×10^14 m^-2 and the average Taylor factor is 3.53 (Fig. 14c and 14f), which underlie the dislocation-strengthening contribution of 414 MPa.
The GA-Extra Trees model showed an average prediction error of 1.56 % across the experimental validation set of the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloy annealed at 750-850 °C.

Fig. 13(c) is captioned 'AN800' but the citing text discusses AN750/AN800/AN850, so this micrograph (predominantly smooth dark ferrite matrix with sparse bright bainitic network) corresponds to the AN850 specimen (likely typographical error in the caption).
